name_en: Linear independence of a sequence of vectors
statement: A sequence of vectors v1,...,vn is linearly independent if the only combination x1v1+...+xnvn that gives the zero vector is the one with all x's equal to zero. Otherwise the vectors are dependent. This definition applies to any sequence of vectors in any vector space.

anchors.quote: DEFINITION The sequence of vectors $v _ { 1 } , \ldots , v _ { n }$ is linearly independent if the only combination that gives the zero vector is
Correct language: "The sequence of vectors is linearly independent." Acceptable shortcut: "The vectors are independent."

name_zh: 矩阵 A 的列无关
statement: The columns of A are linearly independent when the only solution to Ax = 0 is x = 0; no other combination Ax of the columns gives the zero vector. Equivalently the nullspace of A contains only the zero vector.

anchors.quote: DEFINITION The columns of A are linearly independent when the only solution to Ax = 0 is x = 0. No other combination Ax of the columns gives the zero vector.
The columns are independent when the nullspace $N ( A )$ contains only the zero vector.

statement: Vectors are dependent when some combination with x's not all zero gives the zero vector; equivalently one vector is a combination of the other vectors. A sequence of vectors is either dependent or independent.

anchors.quote: If a combination gives 0, when the x's are not all zero, the vectors are dependent.
Note Another way to describe linear dependence is this: "One vector is a combination of the other vectors."
A sequence of vectors is either dependent or independent.

name_en: Independent columns exactly when r = n
name_zh: 列无关当且仅当秩等于 n
statement: The columns of A are independent exactly when the rank is r = n: there are n pivots and no free variables, so only x = 0 is in the nullspace. Independent columns produce full column rank.

anchors.quote: Full column rank The columns of A are independent exactly when the rank is $r = n .$ There are n pivots and no free variables.
The rank is only $r = 2$ . Independent columns produce full column rank $r = n = 3$

name_en: A matrix with m < n has dependent columns
statement: If a matrix has more columns than rows (n > m), its columns are certainly dependent: Ax = 0 has at least n - m free variables and therefore a nonzero solution. Any seven vectors from R^5 are dependent.

anchors.quote: The columns are certainly dependent if $n > m$ , because $A x = \mathbf { 0 }$ has a nonzero solution.
Then the columns must be dependent. Any seven vectors from $\mathbf { R } ^ { 5 }$ are dependent.

statement: A set of vectors spans a space if their linear combinations fill the space. The columns of a matrix span its column space; they might be dependent.

anchors.quote: DEFINITION A set of vectors spans a space if their linear combinations fill the space.
The vectors $v _ { 1 } , \ldots , v _ { r }$ span a space if their combinations fill that space.
The column space is spanned by the columns.

statement: A basis for a vector space is a sequence of vectors that are linearly independent and that span the space: not too many and not too few. A space has infinitely many different bases.

anchors.quote: DEFINITION A basis for a vector space is a sequence of vectors with two properties:
The basis vectors are linearly independent and they span the space.
Two vectors $\mathrm { c a n ' t }$ span all of $\mathbf { R } ^ { 3 }$ even if they are independent.

statement: Every vector v in the space is a combination of the basis vectors because they span the space, and there is one and only one such combination because the basis vectors are independent.

anchors.quote: There is one and only one way to write v as a combination of the basis vectors.
A basis consists of linearly independent vectors that span the space. Every vector in the space is a unique combination of the basis vectors.
Every vector v in the space is a combination of the basis vectors, because they span the space.

statement: The dimension of a space is the number of vectors in every basis for that space. It counts the degrees of freedom in the space; the dimension of R^n is n. We never speak of the rank of a space or the dimension of a basis.

anchors.quote: DEFINITION The dimension of a space is the number of vectors in every basis
The number of vectors, in any and every basis, is the "dimension" of the space.

name_en: All bases for a space have the same number of vectors
name_zh: 同一空间的所有基元素个数相同
statement: If v1,...,vm and w1,...,wn are both bases for the same vector space, then m = n. The proof assumes n > m, writes W = VA with A short and wide, and gets a nonzero solution of Ax = 0, so a combination of the w's would be zero.

anchors.quote: If $\pmb { v } _ { 1 } , \ldots , \pmb { v } _ { m }$ and $w _ { 1 } , \ldots , w _ { n }$ are both bases for the same vector space, then $m = n$
All bases for a space have the same number of vectors. This number of vectors in a basis is the dimension of the space.

statement: The columns of the n by n identity matrix give the standard basis for R^n: i and j in R^2, and i, j, k in R^3. They are independent and they span the space.

anchors.quote: The columns of the 3 by 3 identity matrix are the standard basis $i , j ,$ , k.
The columns of the n by n identity matrix give the "standard basis" for $\mathbf { R } ^ { n }$

statement: The row space of a matrix is the subspace of R^n spanned by its rows: all combinations of the rows. It is the column space of A transpose, and it is a subspace of R^n while the column space lives in R^m.

anchors.quote: DEFINITION The row space of a matrix is the subspace of $\mathbf { R } ^ { n }$ spanned by the rows.
The columns span the column space. Here is a new subspace-which is spanned by the rows.
The row space contains all combinations of the rows. This row space of A is the column space of $A ^ { \mathrm { T } }$

statement: The row space of A is written C(A^T), the column space of A transpose: transposing turns the rows of A into columns, so the same numbers now span a subspace of R^n. The left nullspace is written N(A^T).

anchors.quote: The row space of A is $C ( A ^ { \mathrm { T } } )$ . It is the column space of
Instead of the rows of A, look at the columns of $A ^ { \mathrm { T } }$ . Same numbers, but now in the column space

name_en: Columns of an invertible matrix are a basis for R^n
name_zh: 可逆矩阵的列构成 R^n 的基
statement: The vectors v1,...,vn are a basis for R^n exactly when they are the columns of an n by n invertible matrix. Then Ax = 0 forces x = 0 (independence) and Ax = b is always solvable by x = A^{-1}b (spanning), so R^n has infinitely many different bases.

anchors.quote: The vectors $v _ { 1 } , \ldots , v _ { n }$ are a basis for $\mathbf { R } ^ { n }$ exactly when they are the columns of an n by n invertible matrix.
The columns of every invertible n by n matrix give a basis for $\mathbf { R } ^ { n }$
The only solution to $A x = \mathbf { 0 }$ is $\pmb { x } = \pmb { A } ^ { - 1 } \mathbf { 0 } = \mathbf { 0 }$ . The columns are independent.

statement: To find a basis for the space spanned by given vectors: either make them the rows of A and eliminate, keeping the nonzero rows of R, or put them in the columns of A and eliminate, keeping the pivot columns of A (not of R).

anchors.quote: Question Given five vectors in ${ \bf R } ^ { 7 }$ , how do you find a basis for the space they span?
First answer Make them the rows of A, and eliminate to find the nonzero rows of R.
Eliminate to find the pivot columns (of A not R). Those pivot columns are a basis for the column space.

name_en: Bases for matrix spaces and function spaces
name_zh: 矩阵空间与函数空间的基
statement: Independence, basis and dimension are not restricted to column vectors. The space of all 2 by 2 matrices has dimension 4 and the n by n matrix space has dimension n^2; the solution space of y'' = -y has the two basis functions sin x and cos x, so its dimension is 2.

anchors.quote: The words "independence" and "basis" and "dimension" are not at all restricted to column vectors.
Matrix spaces The vector space M contains all 2 by 2 matrices. Its dimension is 4.
That solution space for $y ^ { \prime \prime } = - y$ has two basis functions: sin x and cos x.

statement: The four fundamental subspaces of an m by n matrix are the row space C(A^T) and nullspace N(A) in R^n, and the column space C(A) and left nullspace N(A^T) in R^m. Two come directly from A and two from A transpose; the rank of A reveals all four dimensions.

anchors.quote: Four Fundamental Subspaces 1. The row space is $C(A^{\mathrm{T}})$, a subspace of $\mathbf{R}^{n}$. 2. The column space is $C(A)$, a subspace of $\mathbf{R}^{m}$.
4. The left nullspace is $N(A^{\mathrm{T}})$, a subspace of $\mathbf{R}^{m}$. This is our new space.
The rank of A reveals the dimensions of all four fundamental subspaces.

statement: The left nullspace of A is the nullspace of A transpose: the solutions y of A^T y = 0, a subspace of R^m. Written y^T A = 0^T the vectors y sit on the left of A and combine the rows of A to give the zero row.

anchors.quote: 4. The left nullspace is $N(A^{\mathrm{T}})$, a subspace of $\mathbf{R}^{m}$.
The vectors y go on the $l e f t$ side of A when the equation is written
The y's in the left nulspace combine the rows to give the zero row.

name_en: Fundamental Theorem of Linear Algebra, Part 1
name_zh: 线性代数基本定理第一部分
statement: For an m by n matrix of rank r: the column space and row space both have dimension r, the nullspace has dimension n - r and the left nullspace has dimension m - r. The rank of A therefore fixes the dimensions of all four fundamental subspaces.

anchors.quote: Fundamental Theorem of Linear Algebra, Part 1
The column space and row space both have dimension r.
The nullspaces have dimensions n - r and m - r.

name_en: Rank Theorem: column rank equals row rank
statement: The number of independent columns equals the number of independent rows: the column space of A has dimension r, the same as the row space. The right reason is that the same combinations of columns are zero for A and for R, since Ax = 0 exactly when Rx = 0.

anchors.quote: Rank Theorem: The number of independent columns =the number of independent rows
2 The column space of A has dimension r. The column rank equals the row rank.

statement: There are n - r free variables, so the dimension of the nullspace is n - r: (dimension of column space) + (dimension of nullspace) = dimension of R^n. The counting rule for A^T is r + (m - r) = m.

anchors.quote: There are $n - r$ free variables, so the dimension of the nullspace is $n - r$ . This is the Counting Theorem
( dimension of column space) + ( dimension of nullspace) = dimension of $\mathbf { R } ^ { n }$
The counting rule for A was $r + ( n - r ) = n$

name_en: The n - r special solutions are a basis for the nullspace
name_zh: n-r 个特解构成零空间的基
statement: There is one special solution for each free variable, so with n variables and r pivots there are n - r of them. They are independent because they contain the identity matrix in the free rows, so they form a basis for the nullspace, which has dimension n - r.

anchors.quote: The nullspace has dimension $n - r$ . The special solutions form a basis
Reason: There is a special solution for each free variable.
The next section shows that the $n - r$ special solutions always give a basis for the nullspace.

name_en: Elimination changes rows but not the row space or nullspace
name_zh: 消元不改变行空间与零空间
statement: A has the same row space as R and the same nullspace as R, with the same dimensions and the same bases, because every row of A is a combination of the rows of R and conversely, and the elimination steps do not change the solutions of Ax = 0.

anchors.quote: 1 A has the same row space as R. Same dimension rand same basis.
Reason: Every row of A is a combination of the rows of R. Also every row of R is a combination of the rows of A. Elimination changes rows, but not row spaces.
3 A has the same nullspace as R Same dimension $n - r$ and same basis

name_en: The r pivot columns of A are a basis for C(A)
name_zh: A 的 r 个主元列构成列空间的基
statement: The pivot columns of A are a basis for its column space: they are independent because they start with the r by r identity matrix, and every free column is a combination of them. The dimension of the column space is r. Note that the pivot columns of A must be used, not those of R.

anchors.quote: Conclusion The r pivot columns of A are a basis for its column space $C ( A )$
The pivot columns are independent, and they span, so they are a basis for C(R).
The pivot columns of A are a basis for its column space.

name_en: The r pivot rows are a basis for the row space
name_zh: r 个主元行构成行空间的基
statement: The r pivot rows of R are a basis for the row space of R and of A (the same space): the nonzero rows of R are independent because in the pivot columns they contain the r by r identity matrix, and they span the row space. The dimension of the row space is r.

anchors.quote: 1. The r pivot rows of Rare a basis for the row spaces of Rand A (same space).
So the r pivot rows are a basis for the row space.
The pivot rows of A are a basis for its row space. So are the pivot rows of its echelon form R.

statement: Every rank one matrix is one column times one row, A = uv^T: every row is a multiple of v^T, which is a basis for the one-dimensional row space, and every column is a multiple of u, which is a basis for the column space.

anchors.quote: Every rank one matrix is one column times one row $A = u v ^ { \mathrm { T } }$
On the left is a matrix with three rows. But its row space only has dimension $= ~ 1$
"The column rank equals the row rank which is l."
